subject: Request: temporary SLA tolerance and onboarding credit for NovaEdge pilot
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@novaedge.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@novaedge.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot request — temporary SLA tolerance and credits

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to move forward with a 12-week pilot starting March 8. We have one last item before we sign the SOW: our infra team has a planned migration in month two that will likely cause a predictable maintenance window and make us unable to meet the standard 99.95% uptime target for a short period.

Can Redwood offer a temporary relaxation of the uptime SLO for the pilot window (we expect a 6–8 hour maintenance window in week 6) and limit the associated service-credit exposure? Specifically we'd like:
- Temporary uptime target of 99.5% for the pilot period only (90 days)
- A cap on any service credits triggered to no more than one month's invoice for the pilot
- A small onboarding/implementation credit to offset our integration work (we were hoping for ~10% of the first invoice)

Attached is the latest SOW draft — the schedule and scope are unchanged. Please let us know what is feasible and whether this needs exec sign-off.

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform
NovaEdge

Attachment: NovaEdge_SOW_draft_v3.pdf
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@novaedge.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@novaedge.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot request — temporary SLA tolerance and credits

Hi Liam — thanks for the clarity and for sharing the SOW. I appreciate the heads-up on the migration window.

I'm escalating to our deal desk and legal to confirm an acceptable commercial and contractual approach. High level — I believe a short-term SLO deviation for a pilot is reasonable if we cap exposure and document the deviation in the SOW addendum. Proposed starting point for discussion:
- Temporary uptime target of 99.5% for the 90-day pilot (from start date)
- Service-credit cap: not to exceed 50% of one monthly invoice for the pilot period (we can discuss the exact %; this is conservative from our side)
- One-time onboarding credit: 10% off the first invoice

Jonas / Sean / Marissa — can you review and advise on legal/finance limits and whether this needs executive (Marissa) sign-off? Liam, once we have internal sign-off we'll provide a redline for the SOW and an SLO addendum.

Irene
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL: NovaEdge — SLO deviation terms review

Irene / Marissa / Sean,

Thanks — I reviewed the proposed terms. A few legal considerations and a recommended commercial framing:

1) Scope and duration: we should explicitly cap the deviation window to the pilot dates and require that the maintenance window be scheduled and mutually agreed on in writing. Phrase: "Temporary SLO deviation limited to the 90-day pilot period, contingent on customer-provided maintenance schedule."

2) Credit cap: 50% of one monthly invoice is steep and could set a precedent. Finance, can we cap at 25% of one monthly invoice for the pilot? Alternatively we can cap credits at $XXk for the pilot (whichever is lower). That keeps our max exposure bounded.

3) Onboarding credit: 10% one-time is fine from a legal POV but needs commercial approval. Recommend we convert that to a one-time invoice credit applied at first billing cycle.

4) Termination / rollback: add language that if customer expands beyond the pilot within 6 months, standard SLOs reapply and previous deviations do not carry forward.

Sean — please confirm whether a 25% cap is acceptable to finance; Marissa, if you are comfortable with that floor, we can surface to the customer and request a signed addendum.

I'll prepare a short SLO_Deviation_Terms.docx redline for the SOW after we decide the cap.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLO_Deviation_Terms.docx
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: NovaEdge — SLO deviation terms review

All,

Finance is comfortable with a capped exposure for a short pilot if we also apply a modest commercial concession. My recommendation:
- Service-credit cap: 25% of one monthly invoice for the pilot (hard cap)
- Onboarding credit: 10% one-time applied to first invoice
- Deal-level discount: 12% off list pricing for first three months of the pilot (to offset migration overhead)

This keeps our worst-case seat relatively bounded and gives the customer a clear economic incentive to proceed. If the customer moves to production or extends the arrangement, we will require a formal SLO amendment and revert to standard credits.

Marissa — this requires your exec sign-off to proceed. If you approve, Irene should send the SLO addendum and updated SOW to the customer for signature and we will log the concession on the HubSpot deal.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Finance Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@novaedge.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 16:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot request — temporary SLA tolerance and credits — Executive approval

Liam — thanks for the patience here and for the clear ask. After review, Redwood will approve the following one-time pilot concessions: 

- Temporary SLO deviation: uptime target adjusted to 99.5% for the 90-day pilot starting March 8, 2027. Customer to provide maintenance schedule in writing for any planned windows.
- Service-credit exposure: capped at 25% of one monthly invoice for the pilot (hard cap).
- One-time onboarding credit: 10% applied to the first invoice.
- Commercial concession: 12% discount off list pricing for the first three months of the pilot.

These concessions are limited to the pilot period only. If NovaEdge converts to production or requests extension, standard SLOs and credit terms will apply unless a formal amendment is approved in writing. Jonas will issue an addendum to the SOW documenting the SLO deviation and credit cap; Irene will send the redlined SOW and addendum for signature and update the HubSpot deal with the approved concessions (DEAL-NE-2027-0421).

Irene — you have exec sign-off to proceed. Please coordinate with Liam on scheduling the maintenance window and upload the signed addendum to the deal record.

Marissa Cole
VP, Sales — Enterprise, Redwood Inference

---
On a related note: Deal Desk, please record the approved concession set and ensure billing applies the one-time credits on first invoice for NovaEdge once the contract executes.


Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@novaedge.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot request — temporary SLA tolerance and credits — Executive approval

Marissa / Irene — this is perfect, thank you. We'll sign the addendum as soon as Jonas sends it and confirm the maintenance window schedule. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Liam
